# statmodels7

[statmodels7](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/) is the
modeling layer of the [statmodels7](https://statmodels7.github.io)
toolkit, and the package that installs the rest of it.
[`statmod()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmod.md)
reads one formula carrying an equation for every parameter of a
distribution and fits it, with any term of
[modelterms7](https://statmodels7.github.io/modelterms7/) in any of
those equations.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("statmodels7/statmodels7")
```

Attaching it attaches the eight member packages.

``` r

library(statmodels7)
#> -- Attaching the statmodels7 toolkit 0.203.3
#> v basis7         0.15.1   v numericals7    0.23.3
#> v distributions7 0.80.2   v optimizers7    0.15.1
#> v linkfunctions7 0.5.4    v parameters7    0.26.0
#> v modelterms7    0.99.3   v penalties7     0.33.0
```

## Fitting a model

The equations are separated by a bar, one for each parameter of the
distribution, and a parameter with no equation of its own is given an
intercept. Below, the mean carries a penalized smooth of `x` and a
random intercept over `g`, and the standard deviation is linear in `x`
on its log scale.

``` r

set.seed(1)
n <- 400
d <- data.frame(x = runif(n, min = -2, max = 2),
                g = factor(rep(1:20, length.out = n)))
u <- rnorm(20, mean = 0, sd = 0.5)
d$y <- sin(2 * d$x) + u[as.integer(d$g)] + rnorm(n, sd = exp(-0.7 + 0.4 * d$x))

fit <- statmod(y ~ s(x) + random(~ 1 | g) | sigma ~ x,
               distrib = gaussian1_distrib(), data = d)
```

The smoothing parameter of the smooth and the scale of the random effect
are hyperparameters. They are estimated by REML, whose gradient and
Hessian are computed exactly, and
[`hyper()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/hyper.md)
reports each value with its source: the criterion that estimated it, or
`fixed` for a value held in the term.

``` r

hyper(fit)
#>   parameter           term   name  estimate  held source   id
#> 1        mu           s(x) lambda 1.3774223 FALSE   reml <NA>
#> 2        mu random(~1 | g)  sigma 0.5804077 FALSE   reml <NA>
```

[`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html) prints the
coefficients and the hyperparameters of each equation, with the
effective degrees of freedom of each penalized term.

``` r

summary(fit)
#> A statmod fit
#> 
#> Call:  statmod(formula = y ~ s(x) + random(~1 | g) | sigma ~ x, distrib = gaussian1_distrib(), 
#>             data = d)
#> 
#> Distribution: gaussian1     Observations: 400
#> 
#> === mu   [identity link]
#> 
#> Parametric terms
#>                estimate     se      z      p   lower  upper
#>   (Intercept)   0.02975 0.1332 0.2234 0.8233 -0.2313 0.2908
#> 
#> s(x)   [9 coefficients, edf 6.81]
#>                  estimate     se    z        p  lower  upper
#>   lambda [reml]     1.377 0.8096               0.4353  4.359
#>   lin              0.2184 0.0354 6.17 6.83e-10 0.1491 0.2878
#> 
#> random(~1 | g)   [20 coefficients, edf 18.45]
#>                 estimate      se  lower  upper
#>   sigma [reml]    0.5804 0.09696 0.4184 0.8052
#>   predicted effects (20 levels of g)
#>                  Min. 1st Qu.   Median Mean 3rd Qu.  Max.
#>     (Intercept)  -1.1 -0.3411 0.008096    0  0.2206 1.151
#> 
#> === sigma   [log link]
#> 
#> Parametric terms
#>                estimate      se      z       p  lower   upper
#>   (Intercept)   -0.6693 0.03661 -18.28 < 1e-16 -0.741 -0.5976
#>   x              0.3736 0.03385  11.04 < 1e-16 0.3072  0.4399
#> 
#> 95% intervals, bayesian variance
#> conditional log-likelihood -282.744059    effective df 28.26
#> cAIC 622.006    cBIC 734.801
#> fitted in 1.99 s
#> inner   max |grad|/se 1.9e-15   min eigen 0.014
#> outer   max |grad|/se 2.9e-12   min eigen 0.97
#> 1 note: print(summary(fit), notes = TRUE)
```

After the conditional log-likelihood and the information criteria, the
table ends with two lines headed `inner` and `outer`. Each gives the
largest gradient in standard errors and the smallest eigenvalue of the
curvature, for the coefficients and for the hyperparameters
respectively, and both are read at the point that the fit reached.

[`statmod_certificate()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmod_certificate.md)
is computed at the same point and not read off the stopping rule of the
optimizer. Its `mode_error` is how far above its own penalized mode the
coefficients stopped, in log-likelihood units, and its `state` is
`converged`, `boundary`, `not converged` or `unknown`.

``` r

statmod_certificate(fit)[c("state", "mode_error")]
#> $state
#> [1] "converged"
#> 
#> $mode_error
#> [1] 4.831658e-30
```

[`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html) returns the fitted
value of any parameter, or of a moment of the response, with a standard
error that follows from every term in the model.

``` r

predict(fit, what = "mu", newdata = head(d, n = 3), se = TRUE)
#>           fit        se      lower      upper
#> 1 -0.81384092 0.1046663 -1.0189830 -0.6086988
#> 2  0.06690214 0.1012942 -0.1316309  0.2654351
#> 3  1.41682665 0.1327520  1.1566376  1.6770157
```

## What the layer fits

Any term of `modelterms7` goes in any equation: the parametric block,
penalized smooths of one and several covariates, grouped random
intercepts and slopes, ridge, lasso, elastic net, SCAD and MCP, a
nonlinear parametric term, effects that change at estimated
break-points, score-driven dynamics and latent Markov regimes. A formula
carries at most one score-driven term, regime term or break-point term
built with `marginal = TRUE`. A score-driven term is fitted in one
system with the coefficients, and
[`vcov()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/vcov.html) is built from the observed
information of that joint model. A regime term, or a marginal
break-point term, is fitted by alternating with the coefficients.

The hyperparameters of a smooth penalty are estimated by
[`reml()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/reml.md)
or
[`ml()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/reml.md),
or by
[`aic()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/aic.md) or
[`bic()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/aic.md) on
an estimate of prediction error, all passed as `outer_criterion`. A
penalty with a kink (`lasso()`, `enet()`, `scad()` and `mcp()`) has no
second derivative at the mode, so its hyperparameter is chosen along a
path of its own values, from the value that empties the block downwards.
The path is scored by `sparse_criterion`, which is
[`bic()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/aic.md) by
default and may also be
[`aic()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/aic.md) or
[`cv()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/cv.md). The
function
[`cv()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/cv.md)
serves only as `sparse_criterion`.

Random effects written with the same label and the same grouping share
one covariance block, in whichever equation they appear, as with the
middle bar of `(1 | u | id)` in `brms`. The formula
`y ~ random(~ 1 | u | id) | sigma ~ random(~ 1 | u | id)` estimates the
correlation between a subject’s level and the logarithm of its scale.
The label reaches a subformula too, so
`seg(x, psi ~ random(~ 1 | u | id))` in the same formula correlates a
random break-point with a random scale. The block is one multivariate
prior over the effects of one level, parametrized by `dr_prod()` by
default, whose free coordinates are the logarithms of the standard
deviations followed by the angles of the correlation.

[`rstatmod()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/rstatmod.md)
simulates from a model written the same way and returns the parameters
used beside the data.

``` r

sim <- rstatmod(y ~ x, distrib = gaussian1_distrib(), data = d[1:20, ],
                par = list(mu = c(1, 2), sigma = log(0.3)))
sim$par
#> $mu
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>           1           2 
#> 
#> $sigma
#> (Intercept) 
#>   -1.203973
```

The vignette [fitting a distributional
model](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/articles/fitting-a-distributional-model.html)
works through a fit from the formula to the fitted object.

## The toolkit in one package

Installing this package installs the eight members, and attaching it
attaches them. The members are listed in `Imports` and attached by the
package itself, which prints one message with the version of each;
`Depends` would attach them without a report.

``` r

statmodels7_packages()
#> [1] "basis7"         "distributions7" "linkfunctions7" "modelterms7"   
#> [5] "numericals7"    "optimizers7"    "parameters7"    "penalties7"
```

| package | what it provides |
|----|----|
| [numericals7](https://statmodels7.github.io/numericals7/) | the numerical layer at the root: stencils, batched quadrature and series, the combinatorial enumerations, special functions |
| [linkfunctions7](https://statmodels7.github.io/linkfunctions7/) | link functions as objects, with exact derivatives to fifth order in both directions |
| [distributions7](https://statmodels7.github.io/distributions7/) | univariate and multivariate distributions with exact score, information and higher derivatives |
| [optimizers7](https://statmodels7.github.io/optimizers7/) | optimization algorithms as objects, with composable stopping rules |
| [basis7](https://statmodels7.github.io/basis7/) | basis expansions with derivatives, anchored integrals and exact Gram matrices |
| [parameters7](https://statmodels7.github.io/parameters7/) | constrained parameters as maps from an unconstrained vector, exact to fourth order |
| [penalties7](https://statmodels7.github.io/penalties7/) | penalties as objects, with exact derivatives, proximal operators and the pieces that a marginal criterion consumes |
| [modelterms7](https://statmodels7.github.io/modelterms7/) | model terms as objects, each carrying its design block, its penalty and its blueprint for new data |

[`statmodels7_versions()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmodels7_versions.md)
reports the installed version of each member,
[`statmodels7_conflicts()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmodels7_conflicts.md)
the names that members mask from one another, and
`statmodels7_update(action = "install")` installs or updates every
member.

## Related

The mathematical companion to the toolkit is the
[book](https://statmodels7.github.io/book/), which presents the formulas
that the packages implement, explains where each quantity comes from and
cites the source of the full argument.

# Package index

## The toolkit

The packages of which the toolkit is made, their versions, and whether
any of their exports mask one another.

- [`statmodels7_packages()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmodels7_packages.md)
  : The Packages of the Toolkit
- [`statmodels7_versions()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmodels7_versions.md)
  : Installed Versions of the Toolkit
- [`statmodels7_conflicts()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmodels7_conflicts.md)
  : Exports of the Toolkit That Mask One Another

## Specifying a model

One formula carries the equations of all the parameters of the
distribution, separated by a bar, and the terms of each equation come
from modelterms7.

- [`statmod_spec()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmod_spec.md)
  : Build a Model Specification
- [`statmod_equations()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmod_equations.md)
  : Split a Multi-Parameter Formula Into One Equation Per Parameter
- [`statmod_design()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmod_design.md)
  : The Design of a Specification

## Fitting

One formula and one distribution. The coefficients of the terms with a
differentiable penalty are fitted in one system, together with a
score-driven term, and the terms with a kinked penalty and the regime
terms are alternated with that system. The section also holds the inner
method, the criteria for the hyperparameters and the simulator.

- [`statmod()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmod.md)
  : Fit a Model
- [`linpar_options()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/linpar_options.md)
  : Options for the Unpenalized Parametric Block
- [`iwls()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/iwls.md)
  [`print(`*`<Iwls>`*`)`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/iwls.md)
  : Iterated Weighted Least Squares
- [`reml()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/reml.md)
  [`ml()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/reml.md)
  : Estimate the Hyperparameters by a Marginal Likelihood
- [`aic()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/aic.md)
  [`bic()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/aic.md)
  : Prediction-Error Criteria for the Hyperparameters
- [`cv()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/cv.md) :
  Choose the Hyperparameters by Cross-Validation
- [`rstatmod()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/rstatmod.md)
  : Simulate a Response From a Written Model
- [`print(`*`<StatmodSim>`*`)`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/print.StatmodSim.md)
  : Printing a Simulation

## The information matrix and the solver

The matrix that the inner fit inverts, that enters a Laplace determinant
or that gives the standard errors is passed as an object: the observed
Hessian and the expected (Fisher) information, both defined in
distributions7, or a choice settled against the family. The
factorization that solves each step is passed as an object too, with its
numerical tolerances.

- [`information_objects`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/information_objects.md)
  : Information Matrices Available to a Fit
- [`auto_info()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/auto_info.md)
  : Information Chosen Against the Family
- [`AutoInfo()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/AutoInfo.md)
  : S7 Class for the Information Chosen Against the Family
- [`iwls_solvers`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/iwls_solvers.md)
  : Solvers Available to a Scoring Step
- [`solve_qr()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/solve_qr.md)
  : The QR Solver
- [`solve_svd()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/solve_svd.md)
  : The SVD Solver
- [`solve_chol()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/solve_chol.md)
  : The Cholesky Solver
- [`IwlsSolver()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/IwlsSolver.md)
  [`SolveQR()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/IwlsSolver.md)
  [`SolveSVD()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/IwlsSolver.md)
  [`SolveChol()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/IwlsSolver.md)
  : S7 Classes for the Solver of a Scoring Step

## Where a fit begins

A starting value given as a strategy and not as a vector of numbers, and
evaluated once before the fit alternates. The default builds the start
from intercept-only fits; the other strategies are procedures, from a
random perturbation to a global search of the likelihood to the
estimates of a model already fitted.

- [`start_strategy()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/start_strategy.md)
  : S7 Class for a Starting-Value Strategy
- [`start_at()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/start_at.md)
  : Where a Fit Begins
- [`start_intercepts()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/start_intercepts.md)
  : Start at the Intercept-Only Fit
- [`start_origin()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/start_origin.md)
  : Start at the Origin
- [`start_random()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/start_random.md)
  : Start From a Random Draw
- [`start_search()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/start_search.md)
  : Search the Likelihood for a Starting Point
- [`start_from()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/start_from.md)
  : Start From Another Fit's Estimates

## Reading a fit

The log-likelihood, gradient and Hessian of the model as functions of
the parameters and the data, the hyperparameters of a fit with their
source, the certificate of convergence, the latent variables of a
structural term, and a duration written in a readable unit.

- [`loglik()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/loglik.md)
  [`gradient()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/loglik.md)
  [`hessian()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/loglik.md)
  : The Model as a Function of Parameters and Data
- [`hyper()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/hyper.md)
  : The Hyperparameters of a Fitted Model
- [`statmod_certificate()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmod_certificate.md)
  : The Certificate of the Reported Point
- [`statmod_latent()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmod_latent.md)
  : The Latent Variables of a Fitted Structural Term
- [`format_duration()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/format_duration.md)
  : Format a Duration in a Readable Unit

## Intervals of a prediction

The argument `interval` of
[`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html) takes an object that
selects the uncertainty that the interval describes: the estimates
alone, the estimates and the effects of a new group, or a new
observation of the response. A prediction interval holds a second object
that sets how the estimation uncertainty enters the predictive
distribution.

- [`predict_intervals`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/predict_intervals.md)
  : Intervals of a Prediction
- [`interval_type()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/interval_type.md)
  : S7 Class for the Interval of a Prediction
- [`confidence_interval()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/confidence_interval.md)
  : The Confidence Interval of a Prediction
- [`group_interval()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/group_interval.md)
  : The Interval of a New Group's Parameter
- [`prediction_interval()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/prediction_interval.md)
  : The Interval of a New Observation
- [`predictive_distributions`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/predictive_distributions.md)
  : Predictive Distributions of a New Response
- [`predictive_type()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/predictive_type.md)
  : S7 Class for the Predictive Distribution of a New Response
- [`pred_averaged()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/pred_averaged.md)
  : Predictive Distribution Averaged Over the Estimates
- [`pred_plugin()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/pred_plugin.md)
  : Plug-in Predictive Distribution
- [`pred_bootstrap()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/pred_bootstrap.md)
  : Parametric Bootstrap Predictive Distribution

## Testing a coefficient

One coefficient against one value, by Wald’s statistic, the likelihood
ratio, Rao’s score or Terrell’s gradient. `summary(test =)` reports the
same four for every row against zero, and `confint(test =)` inverts
them;
[`statmod_test()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmod_test.md)
also takes a null value other than zero. The test that a break-point
exists is a separate function, which reads the supremum of a score
process over the positions of the break-point.

- [`statmod_test()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmod_test.md)
  : Test One Coefficient Against One Value
- [`statmod_breakpoint_test()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmod_breakpoint_test.md)
  : Test That a Break-Point Exists

## Test statistics

The four statistics with which a coefficient is tested, as objects
passed to the argument `test` of
[`statmod_test()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmod_test.md),
[`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html) and
[`confint()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/confint.html): Wald’s, the
likelihood ratio, Rao’s score and Terrell’s gradient. The overview
states the formula of each, what it needs and what it costs, and
[`test_restricted()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/test_restricted.md)
tells whether a statistic refits the model under the restriction.

- [`test_statistic()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/test_statistic.md)
  : Statistics for Testing a Coefficient
- [`wald_test()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/wald_test.md)
  : Wald's Test of a Coefficient
- [`lr_test()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/lr_test.md)
  : Likelihood-Ratio Test of a Coefficient
- [`score_test()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/score_test.md)
  : Rao's Score Test of a Coefficient
- [`gradient_test()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/gradient_test.md)
  : Terrell's Gradient Test of a Coefficient
- [`test_restricted()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/test_restricted.md)
  : Whether a Test Refits the Model Under the Restriction

## Variance conventions

The three conventions for the variance matrix of the coefficients, as
objects passed to the argument `type` of
[`vcov()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/vcov.html),
[`confint()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/confint.html),
[`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html),
[`statmod_test()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmod_test.md)
and [`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html): the Bayesian
variance, the frequentist sandwich, and the unconditional variance that
adds the uncertainty of the hyperparameters.

- [`vcov_method()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/vcov_method.md)
  : Variance Conventions of a Fit
- [`bayesian_vcov()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/bayesian_vcov.md)
  : Bayesian Variance of a Fit
- [`frequentist_vcov()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/frequentist_vcov.md)
  : Frequentist Variance of a Fit
- [`hc0_sandwich()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/hc0_sandwich.md)
  [`hc1_sandwich()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/hc0_sandwich.md)
  : Sandwich Variance of the Coefficients
- [`hc2_sandwich()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/hc2_sandwich.md)
  [`hc3_sandwich()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/hc2_sandwich.md)
  [`hc4_sandwich()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/hc2_sandwich.md)
  : Sandwich Variances with a Leverage Correction
- [`statmod_leverage()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmod_leverage.md)
  : Leverage of the Observations in a Distributional Regression
- [`hac_sandwich()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/hac_sandwich.md)
  : HAC Sandwich Variance of the Coefficients
- [`unconditional_vcov()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/unconditional_vcov.md)
  : Unconditional Variance of a Fit
- [`bootstrap_vcov()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/bootstrap_vcov.md)
  : Bootstrap Variance of a Fit

## Bootstrap

The bootstrap variance of the coefficients: the schemes that resample
the data, the function that stores the refitted replicates in a fit, and
the extractor that reads them.

- [`resample_method()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/resample_method.md)
  : Resampling Schemes for the Bootstrap of a Fit
- [`parametric_resample()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/parametric_resample.md)
  : Parametric Resampling
- [`case_resample()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/case_resample.md)
  : Case Resampling
- [`bayesian_resample()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/bayesian_resample.md)
  : Bayesian Resampling
- [`cluster_resample()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/cluster_resample.md)
  : Cluster Resampling
- [`add_bootstrap()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/add_bootstrap.md)
  : Compute and Store the Bootstrap Replicates of a Fit
- [`statmod_bootstrap()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmod_bootstrap.md)
  : Read the Stored Bootstrap of a Fit
- [`StatmodBootstrap()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/StatmodBootstrap.md)
  : Stored Replicates of a Bootstrap
- [`bootstrap_interval()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/bootstrap_interval.md)
  [`PercentileInterval()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/bootstrap_interval.md)
  [`BasicInterval()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/bootstrap_interval.md)
  [`BcaInterval()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/bootstrap_interval.md)
  [`percentile_interval()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/bootstrap_interval.md)
  [`basic_interval()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/bootstrap_interval.md)
  [`bca_interval()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/bootstrap_interval.md)
  : Bootstrap Intervals for the Coefficients of a Fit

## Graphs of a fit

[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) and
`autoplot()` draw one aspect of a fit as a ggplot2 object. The graph is
selected by an object passed as `type`, and its data are computed by
[`plot_data()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_data.md)
and drawn by
[`plot_layers()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_layers.md),
the two generics through which a new graph is added. Without a type,
[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) draws the
diagnostic graphs of
[`diagnostics()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/diagnostics.md).

- [`autoplot(`*`<StatmodFit>`*`)`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/autoplot.StatmodFit.md)
  [`plot(`*`<StatmodFit>`*`)`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/autoplot.StatmodFit.md)
  : Graphs of a Fitted Model
- [`diagnostics()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/diagnostics.md)
  : Diagnostic Graphs of a Fitted Model
- [`plot_type()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_type.md)
  [`term_plot()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_type.md)
  [`model_plot()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_type.md)
  [`diagnostic_plot()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_type.md)
  : Graphical Types for a Fitted Model
- [`default_plot()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/default_plot.md)
  : The Default Graph of a Term
- [`plot_data()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_data.md)
  : The Data of a Graph
- [`plot_layers()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_layers.md)
  : The Layers of a Graph

## Graphs of a term

Graphs of one term of one equation, selected by `term`: its effect with
the partial residuals, and the graphs that describe a smooth, a
penalized block, a random effect or a structural term.

- [`plot_effect()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_effect.md)
  : Graph of the Effect of a Term
- [`plot_derivative()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_derivative.md)
  : Graph of the Derivative of a Smooth
- [`plot_surface()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_surface.md)
  : Graph of the Surface of a Smooth of Two Variables
- [`plot_criterion()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_criterion.md)
  : Graph of the Outer Criterion Against a Hyperparameter
- [`plot_shrinkage()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_shrinkage.md)
  : Graph of the Shrinkage of a Penalized Block
- [`plot_path()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_path.md)
  : Graph of the Coefficient Paths of a Penalized Block
- [`plot_caterpillar()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_caterpillar.md)
  : Graph of the Predicted Effects of a Random Effect
- [`plot_prior()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_prior.md)
  : Graph of the Prior of a Random Effect
- [`plot_random_cov()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_random_cov.md)
  : Graph of the Covariance of a Random Effect
- [`plot_curves()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_curves.md)
  : Graph of the Curves of a Random Smooth
- [`plot_breakpoint()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_breakpoint.md)
  : Graph of the Break-Points of a Term
- [`plot_filter()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_filter.md)
  : Graph of a Filtered Parameter
- [`plot_news_impact()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_news_impact.md)
  : Graph of the News Impact of a Score-Driven Term
- [`plot_states()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_states.md)
  : Graph of the State Probabilities of a Regime Term
- [`plot_regime_density()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_regime_density.md)
  : Graph of the Density of the Response under Each Regime

## Graphs of the fitted distribution

Graphs of the whole fitted distribution as a function of the covariates,
without a term: a parameter with its band, the conditional quantile
curves, the density at chosen covariate values and the moments.

- [`plot_param()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_param.md)
  : Graph of a Fitted Parameter Against a Covariate
- [`plot_quantiles()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_quantiles.md)
  : Graph of the Conditional Quantiles Against a Covariate
- [`plot_density()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_density.md)
  : Graph of Fitted Densities at Chosen Covariate Values
- [`plot_moments()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_moments.md)
  : Graph of the Moments of the Fitted Distribution Against a Covariate

## Diagnostic graphs

Graphs of the fit against the data, selected without `term`: the
quantile residuals in a quantile-quantile graph, a worm plot, a
histogram of the probability integral transform and a calibration graph,
the residuals against a quantity or in order, the scores and the
influence of the observations, and a comparison with simulated
responses.

- [`plot_qq()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_qq.md)
  : Quantile-Quantile Graph of the Residuals
- [`plot_worm()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_worm.md)
  : Worm Plot of the Residuals
- [`plot_residuals()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_residuals.md)
  : Graph of the Residuals against a Quantity
- [`plot_pit()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_pit.md)
  : Histogram of the Probability Integral Transform
- [`plot_calibration()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_calibration.md)
  : Calibration of the Predicted Quantiles
- [`plot_score()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_score.md)
  : Graph of the Scores of an Equation
- [`plot_influence()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_influence.md)
  : Graph of the Influence of the Observations on an Equation
- [`plot_acf()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_acf.md)
  : Autocorrelation of the Residuals
- [`plot_ppc()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/plot_ppc.md)
  : Comparison of the Response with Simulated Responses

## Installing and updating

The toolkit is not on CRAN, so the install path is GitHub and the
dependencies among the members are resolved by pak.

- [`statmodels7_update()`](https://statmodels7.github.io/statmodels7/reference/statmodels7_update.md)
  : Install or Update the Toolkit

## Internals

The machinery from which the exported functions are built: the classes
behind a fit, the methods registered for the generics of stats, and the
helper functions. Using the package does not require any of it.
